previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and anxiety was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and diabetic ketoacidosis with a blood glucose of 432 and an elevated anion gap. She was treated with IV fluids and insulin, which resolved her DKA. Persistent nausea was managed with antiemetics, and her tachycardia improved. Throughout the stay, she acknowledged that stress related to transitioning to an insulin pump contributed to her symptoms, and she recognized a pattern of self-induced vomiting during episodes. With support from her husband and medical team, she agreed to seek outpatient psychological care. By discharge, she was tolerating a soft diet, had no vomiting, and was stable. She was discharged home with medication adjustments and a plan for follow-up.

# Gastroparesis: Patient presented with nausea and vomiting on 
admission. The etiology was likely related to gastroparesis but 
the trigger was unclear. Her UA was clean and she remained 
afebrile. ___ nurse reported small amount of coffee ground in 
emesis, but otherwise there were no signs of GI bleed. Her HCT 
was at baseline. She received pantoprazole 40 mg IV and 
subsequently PO. PPI was stopped when there was no evidence of 
further GI bleed.  Strong suspicion that bleeding, if present 
was due to ___ tear given transient nature and 
retching.  She also received lorazepam, ondansetron and 
metoclopromide for her nausea and slowly improved.  Her diet was 
slowly advanced from clear liquids to regular diet which she 
tolerated well. Her nausea and vomiting resolved by the time of 
discharge.   

#Diabetes Mellitus I/ Ketoacidosis: Patient had been on insulin 
pump at home but it was removed in the ___.   Unfortunately, 
given NPO status and previous low blood glucose values her 
insulin glargine was held on arrival to floor leading to 
hyperglycemia and the development of an anion gap of 22.  This 
closed quickly with appropriate insulin dosing and no secondary 
cause of hyperglycemia (no infection, ischemia, etc..) was 
found.  Endocrine was consulted and helped manage her insulin 
from that point forward.  She was restarted on her insulin pump 
on morning of discharge with reasonable control.   Her blood 
sugar was 261 at discharge. 

#Hyponatremia: Patient's serum sodium was found to be 130 on 
___. The etiology was likely related to hypovolumia as she 
vomited several times the day prior. She was treated with IV NS 
1000 cc and her discharge sodium level was 133. Other 
electrolytes were repleted as needed. 

#Tachycardia: rate 100s. sinus. similar to prior during last 
admission. chronic issue for patient. 

#Leukocytosis: She had elevated WBC to 15 initially and 
subsequently downtrended to 8.3 at discharge. The etiology was 
unclear. It ___ be stress reaction in setting of gastroparesis 
and elevated glucose. There was no evidence of infection on UA 
or CXR. No localizing symptoms of infection. Blood cultures 
showed no growth at discharge but the final result is pending.

#HTN: initially held home lisinopril given low blood pressure 
but subsequently restarted because her BP was elevated. Her BP 
was WNL at discharge.

#Depression/ anxiety: We continued her home amitryline and 
ativan prn. We initially held her home clonazepam as she was 
receiving frequent ativan, but it was later restarted because 
her ativan use decreased.
